newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* Microsoft to invest $150 million in Apple Computer.
* Columbia/HCA to alter or abandon many controversial business practices.
* Amos Hostetter resigns as U S West executive.
* The U.S. economy is continuing to expand modestly, a Fed report showed.
* Cabletron chief executive to resign and be replaced by Nynex executive.
* Trading in Equisure was halted amid a probe of the company's accounting and trading in its shares.
* U.S. stocks rose sharply, sending major indexes to records.
* A drug abandoned by its maker, Hoechst Marion Roussel, appears to be the first drug to reduce the high rate of angioplasty.
* United Parcel Service and its Teamsters union will meet today.
* A judge release secret tobacco industry documents that reflect discussions among lawyers to supress scientific research and mislead the public.
* Gannett to buy two New Jersey newspapers.
* Some provisions in the new tax law could hurt investors.
* Hilton Hotels boosts offer for ITT.
* PG&E to buy power plants from New England Electric System for $1.59 billion.
* Fed Chairman Greenspan opposes accounting change on derivatives.
